items.title: perf(desktop): bound retained text lines while counting full files
items.body:
## Summary

Retain only the requested prefix of a desktop text file while still counting every line. Apply the same bounded allocation to the TypeScript reader and the emitted Python reader.

## Problem and approach

Both readers currently split the complete retained file into an array before applying the default 5,000-line view budget. A captured 24 MiB text file containing 4,194,304 short lines therefore allocates millions of strings that never appear in the result.

The TypeScript reader scans newline positions and slices only retained lines. The Python reader counts LF separators and takes the requested prefix from the existing line iterator. Empty input, CRLF, final newlines, blank lines, lone CR characters and Unicode line-separator characters keep their existing interpretation.

Semantic owner: the desktop text-view producers. CLI/MCP contracts, line counts, truncation flags, Evidence identity and provenance stay unchanged. This is an optimization within the existing captured-data reader; no new provider or target-execution capability is added.

## Current-main compatibility (2026-11-16)

The existing head `fd997ec1ee` merges cleanly with upstream `836ac2fea6`. On that combined tree, the focused source suites passed: 31 state-format tests, 51 desktop-state application tests, and 22 emitted-Python boundary tests (104 total). The Python parity suite includes the 20,001-line CRLF file with a two-line budget. Changed-file formatting and `git diff --check` also passed. These checks used an isolated installation of the required dependencies; the complete lockfile install and full repository gate were not repeated. The original benchmark below remains the comparison against `653c49419e`; it was not rerun for this compatibility check. The existing green branch head is preserved.

## Executed performance comparison

Compared base `653c49419e65515d5567ebf13c0e6dd2ac794f7e` with this change using a real retained capture and the compiled public command:

```sh
node scripts/rea.mjs inspect-desktop-application-state CAPTURE --format json
```

Three fresh processes per revision, alternating order, warm filesystem cache, Node 24.22.1 on Linux. Medians:

| Measurement | Base | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Completed CLI elapsed time | 2.633 s | 1.927 s |
| Child-family user CPU | 2.020 s | 1.478 s |
| Child-family system CPU | 0.493 s | 0.269 s |
| Peak process-family RSS | 560,484,352 B | 310,145,024 B |
| Peak process-family PSS | 532,666,368 B | 283,750,400 B |

RSS/PSS were sampled every 10 ms. Other repository checks shared the host, so timings are workload observations, not a general throughput guarantee. Every full CLI Evidence result had the same canonical SHA-256 `63a07c507854712757ef026aaa044359650dd6ee095794e0ceac1eb3aba4f7bd` and the same Evidence IDs, 5,000 retained lines, complete count and truncation flag.

The actual emitted Python reader was also run on the same input: median peak process-family RSS changed from 299,954,176 B to 65,417,216 B; normalized results were identical. Token usage was not measured. No browser, Hopper or Ghidra performance claim is made.

## Validation performed

- `npm run test:local -- src/domain/desktop/stateFormats.test.ts src/application/desktop/DesktopApplicationState.test.ts`: 80 passed.
- `npm run test:focused -- tests/boundary/providers/desktopExportPython.test.ts`: runtime and skill artifacts built; 22 passed, including real emitted-Python parity for a 20,001-line CRLF file and a custom two-line budget.
- `npm run check:fast`: typecheck and lint tasks passed with official telemetry opt-out enabled.
- Configured `lint-staged --diff HEAD^ --fail-on-changes` tasks passed for all four changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- The broader `npm run check` attempt passed its typecheck, lint, formatting, knip, metadata and architecture stages, but the final whole-project typed-lint process was killed with SIGKILL. That complete gate did not pass. Changed-file typed lint reported zero errors; a pre-existing parameter-count warning remains outside the changed function.

The correctness controls pass on both revisions; this change fixes allocation cost, not a different text result. No migration, package dependency or release-metadata change is required.

## Contribution ownership

The core contribution bounds retained line allocations in both desktop text-view producers while preserving complete line counts, truncation semantics, and Evidence results.

The source-checkout helper now validates one target, detects unrecognized or repeated flags, checks the two supported target kinds and verifies the JSON array of NUL-free strings. `--help` now prints the invocation. items.title: feat(evidence): paginate retained evidence discovery summaries
items.body:
## Summary

Let callers page the metadata returned by `get_evidence_bundle` and `inspect-evidence-bundle` with `detail: "summary"`. Previously that projection returned every matching row and rejected pagination. Once the summary exceeded the MCP response budget, even identifying the next Evidence ID could require exporting the whole bundle. Selecting full records did not solve the problem for large payloads.

## Behavior and compatibility

- Supplying `offset` or `limit` enables paging. Offsets default to 0 and page size to 64. Apply the existing exact filters first and return rows in canonical Evidence ID order. Follow `page.next_offset` until it is null against an unchanged session or file.
- With neither parameter the existing full summary and output shape are preserved, with no `page` member. Complete bundle, record and link delivery keep their existing semantics.
- `matching_records`, `direct_links` and `missing_direct_links` still cover all matches. Bundle totals and unknown-revision counts keep their original scope. Metadata projection is limited to selected rows except where a procedure filter requires it; computing global counts still scans the matches.
- An oversized summary response now recommends retrying at the same offset with a smaller limit. If one metadata row cannot fit, export is still the recovery path. The portable CLI continues to validate the full bundle before selecting a page.

## Regression evidence

The MCP regression uses 96 retained records and a 16 KiB response budget. Before the change the full summary and one complete record exceeded the budget, and a request for seven summary rows was rejected. The test now follows seven-row pages and recovers all 96 IDs exactly once. It checks actual serialized delivery size, advertised schemas, filtered totals and recovery for a single oversized metadata row.

items.title: fix(process): preserve UTF-8 at diagnostic truncation boundaries
items.body:
## Problem

Byte-bounded command diagnostics can introduce replacement characters into valid UTF-8 output when the retained head or tail cuts through a multibyte character. For example, an eight-byte excerpt of `A🙂...🙂Z` shows broken emoji bytes around the omission marker. A one-shot `StringDecoder.write()` also hides some malformed bytes at the end of the retained head, such as `0xc0`.

Decode the retained head after excluding only a suffix that could still become a valid UTF-8 code point. Preserve invalid lead bytes and already-invalid prefixes, including overlong encodings, surrogates, and values above U+10FFFF. Skip only the possible continuation-byte fragment at the cut edge of the tail. Raw retention stays within the existing byte budget.

Complete output is decoded after joining the head and tail. The non-truncated regression now uses `A🙂`, whose five-byte buffer is split inside the emoji by the three-byte head limit; every two-chunk split and bytewise append must reconstruct the exact original text.

The semantic owner is `BoundedOutputExcerpt`, shared by the bounded command runner's stdout/stderr diagnostics. This corrects an existing process-output boundary without adding an execution capability or changing byte limits, exit codes, or the tail policy.

items.title: fix(contracts): include ref siblings in presentation budgets
items.body:
## Summary

The presentation counter skips schema-valued `$ref` siblings. Under a conservative schema-position policy, 16 properties with both a target reference and an `allOf` reference plus one extra reference contain 33 reference occurrences; the base counts 17 and keeps the shared form at budget 32. This change makes that policy count every supported schema-valued position. The actual Pi versions tested below use only 17 expansions for this sibling fixture, so this is not a reproduced Pi field-loss case.

Continue through schema-valued siblings after following the target. Keep the caller's reference path for siblings, preserve cycle termination, and leave literal default/const/enum/example data opaque. Keep SDK-level selection checks aligned with that policy.

Refs https://github.com/morluto/rea/discussions/3847, candidate 1. This is a separate focused fix.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Owner: input-schema presentation selection, followed by SDK advertisement.
- Existing canonical schemas, operation names, validation authority and default budget remain unchanged. This corrects when the existing inline fallback is selected; it adds no target execution, network or persistence capability.
- The SDK regression checks advertised selection, schema-position counts and canonical validation. Its local counter is a policy check; actual client-renderer behavior is verified separately below.
- Ordinary fix within existing boundaries; no new provider or advance scope decision applies. No package/version or tracked generated-file change.

## Evidence and validation

Pinned Node 24.18.0 / npm 11.16.0 and locked dependencies.

- Source suite: **22 pass**. Against the base, both added regressions fail (1 vs 3 sibling expansions; 4 vs 6 with recursive paths) while 20 existing tests pass.
- Actual in-memory MCP SDK boundary suite: **15 pass**, including listTools after conversion, 32 shared vs 33 inline, Ajv valid/invalid inputs and valid SDK tool calls. The new SDK case fails against the base because the 33-expansion form remains shared.
- Official `npm run compile:termux`, skill/MCP/product catalog generation and portable ledger generation pass. `npm run docs:check:built` passes; README/onboarding consistency tests **5 pass**. The portable ledger explicitly retains two unsupported provider lanes; this does not claim installed-provider coverage.
- `node --max-old-space-size=3072 node_modules/typescript6/lib/tsc.js --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run knip`, `npm run metadata:check`, `npm run verify:architecture-guards`, changed-file formatting, pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` pass.



### Published Pi renderer probe

Executed the shipped `schemaToType`, `renderToolSignature` and `renderDeclarations` from integrity-verified `@earendil-works/pi-codemode` 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 against eight schemas returned by a real MCP SDK 2.3.1 `listTools` exchange: 16 renderer executions on Node 24.18.0 / Zod 4.4.3, without adding a repository dependency.

- Both sibling fixtures (32/33 conservative reference occurrences) render every input field without `unknown`; these Pi versions expand only 16/17 target references and ignore reference siblings.
- An independent direct-reference control reproduces the actual cutoff: 32 references stay typed; the 33rd renders `zz_extra: unknown`. REA's existing inline fallback restores `zz_extra: string` in both versions.
- Pi 1.2.0 renders the sibling fixture's input in 296 characters shared versus 636 inline. The conservative selector can therefore inline earlier than that renderer needs; no field-loss repair or efficiency gain is claimed for the sibling fixture.

Pinned renderer sources: [1.1.0](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/abe508e1b89912adde45528136c3221eb69acdd7/packages/codemode/src/declarations.ts#L255-L267) and [1.2.0](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/06a466935536f8c9bcacb2d5efc0fc021be1bdff/packages/codemode/src/declarations.ts#L176-L188). This isolates published renderer behavior after SDK conversion; an interactive Pi host/model session remains unverified.

**Limits:** the standard `npm run check` stops in the pinned native TypeScript 7 compiler because this host lacks `/proc/self/exe`; a passing native gate is not claimed. A whole-repository format attempt in this environment also fails in untouched HTML workers at `uv_resident_set_memory`; the three changed TypeScript files pass. SDK loopback and isolated renderer checks do not establish an interactive Pi/client session, a full CLI/provider workflow, performance gains or full CI coverage.




## Current-main status

Superseded by [5e30969](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/5e30969cc5f1255d44ec7a1f1ca8dbac0af5e7c4), which inlines advertised inputs at their projection owner and removes the reference-budget mechanism and tests. This patch no longer applies to current main; resolving its conflicts by restoring the deleted counter would revive a superseded representation. The validation above describes the historical branch, not current-main acceptance. Details: https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3920#issuecomment-6201011007

items.title: fix(setup): deduplicate selected clients before planning
items.body:
## Summary

Repeated `--client` selections currently produce duplicate setup actions. With `--client cursor --client codex --client cursor`, the second Cursor configuration can overwrite its reported result, obscuring the operation that actually ran. Normalize selected identities once in `runSetupWorkflow`, preserving first-selected order before planning, default skill selection, readiness and apply.

Refs https://github.com/morluto/rea/discussions/3847, candidate 20. This is an independently reviewable fix, separate from the other candidates.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Owner: initial client selection in the shared application workflow; covers CLI and direct callers without a downstream repair.
- Ordinary fix within existing setup authority; no new provider or advance scope decision applies.
- Existing CLI/MCP shapes and registration formats remain; duplicate selections now produce one ordered action and one truthful result per client.
- Setup still reads and, only under its existing approval path, writes selected configuration files. Tests use isolated HOME/USERPROFILE paths with skill/Hopper installation disabled. Actual client launches and provider installation were not exercised.
- Package/release metadata and tracked generated files are unchanged.

## Evidence and validation

Node 24.18.0, npm 11.16.0; locked dependencies.

- New direct-workflow regressions against the base: **2 fail / 23 existing pass**, with repeated action IDs. Patched source: **25 pass**.
- Official `npm run compile:termux` and skill generation pass. The exact test runner then passes **26 tests**, including a real compiled CLI dry-run/apply/rerun journey: unique ordered actions, no-write preview, configured statuses and unchanged repeat execution.
- `node --max-old-space-size=3072 node_modules/typescript6/lib/tsc.js --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run knip`, `npm run metadata:check`, `npm run verify:architecture-guards`, changed-file formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Test discovery finds all 1,318 files exactly once.
- Prepared `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts` passes after the official JavaScript build and skill freshness check (1,671 files). A prepared package-verifier run with process-scoped `npm_config_ignore_scripts=true` passes archive, isolated installation/update, MCP startup/module loading and discovery stages, then fails during artifact-stage cleanup with ENOTEMPTY. Its remaining setup/uninstall/evidence stages are **not verified**; the exact owned test directory was subsequently removed successfully.

**Gate limitations:** standard `npm run check`, `npm run verify:package` and ordinary `npm pack --dry-run` cannot complete here: the pinned native TypeScript 7 compiler panics because `/proc/self/exe` is unavailable. The full repository format check also fails in untouched HTML workers because `uv_resident_set_memory` is unavailable; changed TypeScript files pass formatting. A 2 GiB JavaScript typecheck attempt exhausted its heap; the bounded 3 GiB run above passes. These fallback checks do not establish a passing native gate or full package verifier. No real Cursor/Codex application or optional provider run is claimed. Telemetry is disabled for subsequent checks.
